correctness.rationale: For positive a,T,W,κ,p, the return map of two equal half-period affine-growth-and-impulse stages contracts by e^{-κ(r1^p+r2^p)}<1. Solving the fixed point and integrating its two dry pieces gives aT/4(1+s1)(1+s2)/(1-s1s2). Substitution yields the two claimed hyperbolic means. Setting c=2^(p-1)>1/2 and G=coth(x/2)/coth(cx), differentiation gives (log G)′=-1/sinh(x)+2c/sinh(2cx)<0 from strict growth of sinh(z)/z. The limits are 2^p and 1, proving all strict and equality regimes, including p=1. For p=2 the crossover reduces to cosh^2 x-cosh x-1=0, with unique positive solution. The code at this package’s checker.py independently reconstructed recurrence and tested 38,553 assertions; finite assertions are not a proof.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns the exact stationary time-mean of a surface stock with continuing deposition and two alternative fixed-total-rain event-size allocations. The directly read hydrological source describes buildup, event wash-off and numerical management; three highly relevant published mathematical records instead treat (i) finite-horizon order of three fixed wash-off rates, (ii) stationary renewal timing with fixed per-event retention, and (iii) a different Hill-function allocation objective. The dose-dependent retention and two prescribed periodic rain schedules are not recovered by substitution from those claims. The same-model assessment finds no known direct implication, without claiming exhaustive historical uniqueness. The inaccessible primary paper is an explicit priority risk.
residual_risks: Full main article and appendices of Mao et al. (2024) were not readable, though the abstract was; an equivalent periodic-depth-allocation theorem not mentioned in its abstract cannot be ruled out.
Older rain-wash modeling and general impulsive dynamical optimization could contain this coth phase diagram as an unindexed special case.
The superlinear dose law is hypothetical and its field plausibility requires independent parameter calibration; the present mathematical finding is not an empirical result.

value.rationale: A natural fixed-total-rain choice between one concentrated precipitation event and two equal periodic events involves opposing operational mechanisms: a single stronger event may remove a larger fraction, whereas shorter dry accumulation gaps favor splitting. The full p>0 phase diagram, unique dimensionaless crossover for p>1 and explicit quadratic golden-ratio threshold distinguish these prescriptions analytically; the result is not merely an arbitrary single numerical point. It does not claim global scheduling optimality, total pollutant export reduction or field calibration, preventing misleading management recommendations. It provides a motivated benchmark for a family of event-response laws and reveals exactly when equal splitting cannot be assumed superior.
